newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ to continue JGB buying if necessary - governor.
newsitem.headline: BOJ to continue JGB buying if necessary - governor.

text.p: BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday the central bank will continue outright purchases of Japanese government bonds if necessary.
"We will continue to do so if there is a need," he told a news conference.
"If it's not necessary we will not do it," he said.

Matsushita also said he hoped the government would start reviewing the system of central bank buying of financing bills issued by the government at very low rates. The funds from the bills are used to finance government foreign exchange intervention.

He said it would be favourable to review this system from the standpoint that such bills should basically be absorbed by the market. At the same time, he said the system should also be reviewed from the standpoint of securing necessary funds for the state treasury.
He also called for broad discussion over the government's investment and loan programme which is financed by such items as postal savings.
He urged postal savings, which are a big recipient of deposits and have slightly higher interest rates than private banks, to not hinder the activities of private financial institutions.
